text: [B23HS1101 COMMUNICATIVE ENGLISH SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23HS1101 Category: HS Credits: 2 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: COMMUNICATIVE ENGLISH (Common to all Engineering branches). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Lesson: HUMAN VALUES: Gift of Magi (Short Story). Listening: Topic identification & details. Speaking: Self-introduction & general questions. Reading: Skimming & Scanning. Writing: Mechanics of Writing (Capitalization, Punctuation, Parts of Sentences). Grammar: Parts of Speech, Sentence Structures. Vocabulary: Affixes, Root words, Synonyms, Antonyms. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Lesson: NATURE: The Brook by Alfred Tennyson (Poem). Listening: Main and supporting ideas. Speaking: Group discussions & short talks. Reading: Sequence of ideas. Writing: Paragraph writing. Grammar: Cohesive devices, Articles, Prepositions. Vocabulary: Homonyms, Homophones, Homographs. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Lesson: BIOGRAPHY: Elon Musk. Listening: Global comprehension & summarizing. Speaking: Pair discussions & reporting. Reading: Context-specific clues. Writing: Summarizing, Note-making, Paraphrasing. Grammar: Tenses, Subject-Verb Agreement. Vocabulary: Words often confused, Jargons. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Lesson: INSPIRATION: The Toys of Peace by Saki. Listening: Predictions in conversations. Speaking: Role plays. Reading: Graphical representation & info transfer. Writing: Letter Writing (Official Letters, Resume). Grammar: Direct/Indirect speech, Active/Passive Voice. Vocabulary: Compound words, Collocations. Unit-V (10 Hrs): Lesson: MOTIVATION: The Power of Intrapersonal Communication. Listening: Key terms & concepts. Speaking: Formal oral presentations. Reading: Reading comprehension. Writing: Structured essays. Grammar: Text editing & error correction. Vocabulary: Technical Jargons. Textbooks: Pathfinder: Communicative English (Orient BlackSwan 2023), Empowering with Language (Cengage 2023).

[B23BS1101 LINEAR ALGEBRA & CALCULUS SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23BS1101 Category: BS Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: LINEAR ALGEBRA & CALCULUS. Unit-I (10 Hrs): Matrices: Rank of a matrix by Echelon & Normal form. Inverse by Gauss-Jordan method. System of linear equations: Homogeneous & Non-Homogeneous equations, Gauss elimination method, Jacobi & Gauss Seidel Iteration Methods. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Eigen values, Eigenvectors & Orthogonal Transformation: Properties of Eigen values & Eigenvectors, Diagonalization, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem, Inverse & Power of matrix using Cayley-Hamilton, Quadratic forms, Canonical forms by Orthogonal Transformation. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Calculus & Mean Value Theorems: Rolle's Theorem, Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem, Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem, Taylor's and Maclaurin's series with remainders. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Partial Differentiation & Applications: Functions of several variables, Continuity, Differentiability, Partial & Total derivatives, Chain rule, Directional derivative, Jacobians, Maxima & Minima of two variables, Lagrange multipliers. Unit-V (10 Hrs): Multiple Integrals: Double integrals, Change of order of integration, Triple integrals, Change of variables to polar, cylindrical & spherical coordinates, Finding areas & volumes. Textbooks: Higher Engineering Mathematics by B.S. Grewal (44th Ed), Advanced Engineering Mathematics by Erwin Kreyszig (10th Ed).

[B23BS1103 CHEMISTRY SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23BS1103 Category: BS Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: CHEMISTRY (For AIDS, AIML, CSBS, CSG & CIC). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Electrochemistry & Applications: Electrodes, Calomel electrode, Primary cells (Zinc-air), Secondary cells (Lithium-ion battery), Fuel cells (Hydrogen-Oxygen, PEMFC), Potentiometric & Amperometric sensors. Corrosion: Dry corrosion, Pilling-Bedworth ratio, Electrochemical theory, Galvanic & Differential aeration corrosion, Cathodic protection (Sacrificial anodic, Impressed current), Galvanizing, Tinning, Electroplating. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Modern Engineering Materials: Semiconductors (Intrinsic, Extrinsic, Compound), Solar Cell construction & working, Superconductors (Type-1 & Type-2), Nanomaterials (Sol-gel, Chemical precipitation, Plant-derived synthesis, Applications in catalysis, medicine, sensors). Unit-III (10 Hrs): Structure & Bonding Models: Schrodinger Wave equation, Psi & Psi^2, Particle in 1D box, Molecular Orbital Theory (O2, CO, N2 energy diagrams), Pi-molecular orbitals of butadiene and benzene, Bond order. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Polymer Chemistry: Chain growth polymerization, Plastics (PVC, Teflon, Bakelite, Nylon-6,6, Kevlar), Elastomers (Buna-S, Buna-N), Conducting polymers (Polyacetylene, Polyaniline), Biodegradable polymers (PGA, PLA). Unit-V (10 Hrs): Instrumental Methods & Water Analysis: Beer-Lambert's law, UV-Visible Spectroscopy, IR Spectroscopy, Hard water & Soft water, EDTA method for total hardness, Winkler's method for Dissolved Oxygen. Textbooks: Engineering Chemistry by Jain & Jain (16th Ed), Text book of Applied Chemistry by IV Kasi Viswanath.

[B23CS1101 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING (C LANGUAGE) SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23CS1101 Category: ES Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING (C Language). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Introduction to Computers & Programming: Basic organization of computer, Flowcharts, Algorithms, Pseudocode. C Basics: Data types, Keywords, Variables, Constants, Format Specifiers, Operators (Arithmetic, Relational, Logical, Assignment, Increment/Decrement, Bitwise, Special), Precedence & Associativity, Type conversion. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Control Structures: Decision Making (Simple if, if-else, nested if, else-if ladder, Switch-Case). Looping Statements (While, Do-while, For loops, Nested loops, Break and Continue). Unit-III (10 Hrs): Arrays & Strings: 1D & 2D Arrays, Bubble Sort, Insertion Sort, Selection Sort, Linear Search, Binary Search, Matrix Operations (Addition, Multiplication, Transpose). Strings: String handling functions, string copy & concatenation without library functions. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Structures, Unions & Pointers: Structure definition, accessing elements, Array of structures, Pointer to structure, Unions vs Structures, Bit fields. Pointers: Dereferencing, Pointer arithmetic, Array access using pointers. Unit-V (10 Hrs): Functions & File Handling: Call by value, Call by reference, Passing arrays to functions, Dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc, free), Command line arguments. File Handling: File modes, Reading & Writing files, Random file access, Macros. Textbooks: The C Programming Language by Kernighan & Ritchie, Schaum's Outline of Programming with C by Byron Gottfried.

text: [B23CS1203 DATA STRUCTURES SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23CS1203 Category: PC Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: DATA STRUCTURES (Common to AI&DS, CSE, IT, CSBS, etc). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Linear Data Structures & Algorithm Analysis: Definition & importance of ADTs, Time & Space complexity overview. Searching: Linear & Binary Search. Sorting: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Linked Lists: Singly Linked Lists (representation & operations), Doubly Linked Lists, Circular Linked Lists. Applications: Polynomial expression representation, addition & multiplication, Sparse matrix representation. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Stacks: Stack ADT, Array & Linked List implementations, Applications (Infix to Postfix conversion, Postfix evaluation, Backtracking, Reversing list). Unit-IV (8 Hrs): Queues & Deques: Queue ADT, Array & Linked list implementations, Circular Queues, Priority Queues, BFS traversal. Deques (Double-ended Queues), Palindrome checking. Unit-V (12 Hrs): Trees & Hashing: Trees, Binary Search Tree (BST) insertion, deletion & traversals. Hashing: Hash functions, Collision resolution (Chaining, Open Addressing), Hash tables, Caching applications. Textbooks: Fundamentals of Data Structures in C by Horowitz & Sahni, Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis in C by Mark Allen Weiss.

[B23BS1202 ENGINEERING PHYSICS SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23BS1202 Category: BS Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: ENGINEERING PHYSICS. Unit-I (10 Hrs): Wave Optics: Interference in thin films, Newton's Rings. Diffraction: Fresnel & Fraunhofer diffractions, Single slit, Double slit, Diffraction Grating, Dispersive & Resolving power. Polarization: Double refraction, Nicol's Prism, Half & Quarter wave plates. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Crystallography & X-Ray Diffraction: Space lattice, Unit cell, Bravais lattices, Packing fraction (SC, BCC, FCC), Miller indices, Bragg's law, X-ray Diffractometer, Powder method. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Dielectric & Magnetic Materials: Dielectric polarizability, Clausius-Mosotti equation, Dielectric loss. Magnetic materials: Dia, Para, Ferro, Antiferro, Ferri magnetism, Hysteresis curve, Soft & Hard magnetic materials. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Quantum Mechanics & Free Electron Theory: Dual nature of matter, Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, Schrodinger time independent wave equation, Particle in 1D box. Classical & Quantum free electron theory, Fermi energy, Fermi-Dirac distribution. Unit-V (10 Hrs): Semiconductors: Intrinsic & Extrinsic semiconductors, Fermi level, Drift & Diffusion currents, Einstein's equation, Hall Effect & applications. Textbooks: A Textbook of Engineering Physics by M.N. Avadhanulu & P.G. Kshirsagar, Engineering Physics by D.K. Bhattacharya.

text: [B23HS2101 UNIVERSAL HUMAN VALUES-II SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23HS2101 Category: HS Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: UNIVERSAL HUMAN VALUES-II: UNDERSTANDING HARMONY AND ETHICAL HUMAN CONDUCT (Common to all Programmes of Engineering). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Introduction to Value Education & Self Exploration: Need, Basic Guidelines, Content and Process for Value Education. Self-Exploration: Content and Process, Natural Acceptance, Experiential Validation, Continuous Happiness and Prosperity. Unit-II (10 Hrs): Harmony in the Human Being (Self and Body): Understanding Human Being as Co-existence of Self ('I') and Body. Harmony of 'I' with Body: Sanyam and Health, Correct Appraisal of Physical Needs. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Harmony in the Family and Society: Understanding Harmony in Family (Basic unit of human interaction), Trust (Vishwas) and Respect (Samman) as Foundational Values, Justice in Human Relationships, Extension of Family Values to Society (Undivided Society, Universal Human Order). [B23BS2101 DISCRETE MATHEMATICS & GRAPH THEORY SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23BS2101 Category: BS Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: DISCRETE MATHEMATICS AND GRAPH THEORY (Common to CSE, CSBS, AIML, IT, AIDS, CSG, CIC, CSIT). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Mathematical Logic: Propositional Calculus (Statements, Connectives, WFF, Truth Tables, Tautologies, Duality Law, Normal Forms, Rules of Inference, Consistency). Predicate Calculus (Predicates, Quantifiers, Free & Bound Variables). Unit-II (10 Hrs): Set Theory, Relations & Functions: Operations on Sets, Inclusion-Exclusion. Relations: Properties, Equivalence relations, Partial Ordering, Hasse Diagrams, Lattices. Functions: Bijective, Composition, Inverse, Permutation, Recursive functions. Unit-III (12 Hrs): Combinatorics & Recurrence Relations: Counting principles, Permutations & Combinations, Circular & Restricted permutations, Binomial & Multinomial Theorems. Recurrence Relations: Generating functions, Solving homogeneous & inhomogeneous recurrence relations. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Graph Theory: Graphs, Subgraphs, Adjacency & Incidence matrices, Isomorphic graphs, Paths, Circuits, Eulerian & Hamiltonian graphs. Unit-V (8 Hrs): Multi Graphs & Trees: Bipartite & Planar graphs, Euler's Theorem, Graph coloring, Chromatic number. Trees: Spanning trees, BFS & DFS spanning trees, Prim's and Kruskal's Algorithms. Textbooks: Discrete Mathematical Structures with Applications to Computer Science by Tremblay & Manohar, Discrete Mathematics for Computer Scientists by Mott, Kandel & Baker.

text: [B23IT2101 DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (DBMS) SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23IT2101 Category: PC Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (DBMS). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Introduction: Database system vs File system, Users, Architecture (3-tier), Schema, Instance, ER Model (Entities, Attributes, Relationships, ER Diagrams, Specialization, Generalization). Unit-II (8 Hrs): Relational Model & SQL: Relational Algebra & Calculus. Basic SQL: DDL, DML operations (Create, Alter, Insert, Delete, Update), Constraints (Domain, Key, Integrity). Unit-III (10 Hrs): Structured Query Language: Complex SQL Queries, Select & Where clauses, Joins, Grouping, Aggregation, Sub-queries, Views, Set operations. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Schema Refinement (Normalization): Functional Dependencies, Normal Forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, 4NF, 5NF), Lossless Join & Dependency Preservation. Unit-V (12 Hrs): Transaction Management & Indexing: ACID properties, Serializability, Concurrency control (Lock-based, Timestamp-based, Optimistic), Deadlocks, Recovery. Indexing: B+ Trees, Hash Indexing. Textbooks: Database Management Systems by Raghu Ramakrishnan & Johannes Gehrke, Database System Concepts by Silberschatz, Korth & Sudarshan.

[B23IT2102 OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING THROUGH JAVA SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23IT2102 Category: PC Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING THROUGH JAVA. Unit-I (10 Hrs): Program Structure in Java: Tokens, I/O operations (Scanner), Data Types, Operators, Control Statements (if-else, switch, loops). Unit-II (10 Hrs): Classes, Objects & Methods: Class declarations, Constructors, Overloading, Access Control, Keyword 'this', Wrapper classes (Autoboxing/Unboxing), Static & Final attributes. Unit-III (10 Hrs): Arrays, Inheritance & Interfaces: 1D/2D Arrays, Inheritance types, 'super' keyword, Method Overriding, Abstract Classes, Interfaces, Default & Static methods, Annotations. Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Packages, Exception Handling & Multithreading: User-defined Packages. Exceptions: try, catch, finally, throw, throws, Custom Exceptions. Multithreading: Thread class, Runnable interface, Synchronization. Java I/O streams. Unit-V (10 Hrs): String Handling, JDBC & JavaFX: String & StringBuffer classes. JDBC Architecture, Database connection, ResultSet. JavaFX GUI: Scene Builder, Layouts, Event handling. Textbooks: JAVA One Step Ahead by Anitha Seth & B.L. Juneja, Joy with JAVA by Debasis Samanta.

text: [B23AD2101 ADVANCED DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHM ANALYSIS SYLLABUS] (college): Course Code: B23AD2101 Category: PC Credits: 3 CIE: 30 SEE: 70 Exam: 3 Hrs. Course: ADVANCED DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHM ANALYSIS (For AI & DS). Unit-I (10 Hrs): Advanced Trees: AVL Trees (Creation, Insertion, Deletion, Applications), B-Trees (Operations & Applications), Heap Trees (Min & Max Heaps, Priority Queues). Unit-III (10 Hrs): Greedy & Dynamic Programming: Greedy: Job Sequencing, Knapsack Problem, Minimum Cost Spanning Trees, Single Source Shortest Path. Dynamic Programming: All-Pairs Shortest Path (Floyd-Warshall), Bellman-Ford, 0/1 Knapsack, Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP). Unit-IV (10 Hrs): Backtracking & Branch and Bound: Backtracking: 8-Queens Problem, Sum of Subsets, Graph Coloring. Branch & Bound: 0/1 Knapsack, TSP. Unit-V (10 Hrs): NP-Hard & NP-Complete Problems: Cook's theorem, Clique Decision Problem, Chromatic Number Problem, Job Shop Scheduling. Textbooks: Fundamentals of Data Structures in C++ by Horowitz, Sahni & Mehta, Computer Algorithms in C++ by Horowitz, Sahni & Rajasekaran.

[SRKREC.AC.IN DEPARTMENTS CSE] (college): Established in 1991, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering has grown from an initial intake of 40 students into a premier academic and research hub with a current B.Tech (CSE) intake of 300. Recognized as a Research Centre by JNTU Kakinada since 2019, the department also offers an M.Tech program in Computer Science and Technology. Supported by experienced faculty, specialized laboratories, E-classrooms, and ICT-enabled infrastructure, the department provides a dynamic and student-centric learning environment. The curriculum is aligned with global technological trends and AICTE guidelines, offering specializations in AI/ML and IoT, along with Honors and Minor programs. Strong industry collaborations with organizations such as TCS iON, Netenrich, and Bennett University enhance practical exposure and employability. The department consistently achieves excellent placement records with top salary packages. Professional bodies like ISTE and the Association of Computer Engineers (ACE) further promote technical, co-curricular, and leadership excellence among students. We are committed to providing a high-quality, vibrant learning environment backed by state-of-the-art laboratories and smart classrooms. Our curriculum builds strong foundations in core computing while offering robust exposure to emerging technologies like AI, Machine Learning, Cyber Security, and Cloud Computing. Recognized as a Research Centre by JNTU Kakinada, the department offers M.Tech and doctoral programs, actively driving innovation through industry partnerships, hackathons, and project-based learning. Nurtured by student professional bodies, our graduates excel in global placements, emerging as competent, ethical, and socially responsible engineers. text: [SRKREC.AC.IN DEPARTMENTS ASH INDIAN KNOWLEDGE TRADITIONS] (college): The Division of Humanities offers special study units and seminars focused on the traditional Indian sciences, architecture, mathematics, and philosophical values as part of the holistic engineering curriculum. The Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) curriculum intends to bridge historical Indian contributions in science, engineering, and metallurgy with modern mathematical tools and methods. By doing so, it helps students develop a balanced understanding of classical methodologies and their modern applications in various technological disciplines. Srujana Vatika is a unique initiative of SRKR Engineering College that serves as a vibrant centre for preserving, promoting, and experiencing India's rich heritage of knowledge, culture, and sustainable living. Conceived as a living laboratory of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), it provides students with opportunities to connect with India's timeless traditions through experiential learning. The centre hosts workshops on traditional food practices, awareness programmes on Indian culture, educational visits for school students, and interactions with eminent scholars and national leaders. It also supports the integration of IKS into higher education through faculty training, academic programmes, and research initiatives, nurturing a deep appreciation of India's knowledge traditions while inspiring innovation rooted in cultural wisdom. The initiative is further strengthened by Dr. Satish Kumar Nadimpalli, who is a UGC and AICTE Recognized Master Trainer in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) and a UGC Resource Person for IKS, IKS Division, Ministry of Education, Government of India. As one of the select Master Trainers from Andhra Pradesh, he actively contributes to the promotion and integration of IKS through training, research, and academic outreach.
